question: What is the main difference between a normal and a maladaptive personality pattern?

options.A: Maladaptive patterns only appear in elderly patients with acute physical infections

question: Which outside group is most important for a school to partner with when planning student immunizations?

question: What is the proper thing to do with dirty bedsheets right after removing them from a patient's bed?

question: What must mothers avoid putting on a newborn baby's umbilical cord stump?

question: What is the main goal of day and night hospital services?

question: Why could it backfire if you only consult wealthy community elites when planning a health project?

question: Why is getting enough sleep so important for our patients in the hospital?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will be discharged within forty-eight hours

options.C: It prevents patients from talking too much to the nursing staff
options.D: It speeds up physical healing and strengthens the body's immune defenses

question: What is one of the main ways community health nurses use incidence data?

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when treating young children with HIV?

question: What usually happens to a hospital when its budget is slashed during an economic recession?

question: Which of these is a key intervention used by modern psychiatric nurses?

options.A: Strict physical confinement in isolated cells

options.C: Therapeutic communication and psychoeducation
options.D: Withholding food to enforce behavioral change

question: Why is cost-effectiveness a major factor when choosing essential drugs?

question: What is the main goal of using triage protocols during a mass casualty event?

question: What type of variation is expected, normal, and just part of everyday clinical processes?

question: What is the name of the slippery mass of food formed in the mouth before swallowing?

question: What substance is put into a vaccine to trigger the body's immune defense?

question: Why is proper ergonomic design particularly important for healthcare professionals?

options.D: It prevents physical fatigue and long-term musculoskeletal injuries

question: Why is it helpful to connect medication benefits to personal goals, like going to work or playing with grandchildren?

question: A patient walks into the clinic with a mild ankle sprain and stable vital signs. What triage level fits best?

question: What is the key feature of appropriate technology in primary health care?

question: What does the term 'intervention fidelity' mean in community nursing?

question: Which of these is a major challenge to quality assurance in many Nigerian healthcare settings?

question: If a patient suddenly cannot move their leg due to a spinal injury, which part of the spinal grey matter is likely damaged?

options.A: Dorsal horn
options.B: Lateral horn
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral horn

explanation: Think of the ventral (front) horn as the exit route for movement. It houses the motor neuron cell bodies that send direct signals to your skeletal muscles to make them move. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h3)

question: A nurse accidentally gives the wrong dose because two different drugs have almost identical labels. In a Just Culture, how is this viewed?

question: Why does hyperglycemia occur in patients with diabetes mellitus?

question: Why is it ineffective to impose health programs on a community without their input?

question: Why do nurses prefer using standardized checklists instead of casual chats when checking ward safety?

question: How do staff shortages at primary health centers negatively affect immunization coverage?

question: Why are cooking demonstrations more effective than simply handing out printed pamphlets?

question: Why should you gently swirl a mixed vaccine vial instead of shaking it hard?

options.A: Gentle swirling makes the liquid change colors faster
options.B: Vigorous shaking creates foam and can break down fragile vaccine proteins
options.C: Shaking causes the glass vial to shatter inside the syringe
options.D: Shaking releases dangerous toxic gases into the clinic air

explanation: Think of vaccine proteins like delicate structures—shaking them too hard tears them apart and ruins the medication! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h4)

question: What does the popular research acronym IMRAD stand for?

options.A: Inquiry, Materials, Recording, And Documentation
options.B: Introduction, Methods, Results, And Discussion
options.C: Investigation, Measurement, Review, And Data
options.D: Interpretation, Management, Research, And Draft

explanation: Think IMRAD: Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. It is the golden standard structure for organizing research papers! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical duty of a nurse working in a community mental health center?

options.A: Administering long-acting injectable psychiatric medications
options.B: Performing major neurosurgery for treatment-resistant depression
options.C: Connecting vulnerable clients with local housing and food resources
options.D: Providing psychoeducation to patients and their family members

explanation: Nurses in community settings do not perform neurosurgery; their role focuses on support, education, medication management, and resource linkage. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the purpose of food security early warning systems?

options.A: To predict exact rainfall amounts for the next ten years
options.B: To stop international trade negotiations permanently
options.C: To warn citizens about high prices in luxury restaurants
options.D: To detect impending food shortages before famine strikes

explanation: Early warning systems monitor data so authorities can respond before a crisis becomes a full-scale famine. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h7)

question: What is almost always the very first test a nurse or doctor will order for a woman of childbearing age with secondary amenorrhoea?

options.A: Brain MRI
options.B: Endometrial biopsy
options.C: Karyotype analysis
options.D: Pregnancy test

explanation: Pregnancy is the most common reason a period stops, so we always check this first before running more complex tests! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h5)

question: What should the nurse do before bringing a meal tray to a patient who needs feeding help?

options.A: Restrict all fluids until the meal is finished
options.B: Clear the bedside table and clean your hands
options.C: Give a sleeping pill to calm them down
options.D: Insist that family members feed every meal

explanation: Spot on! Basic hygiene and a clean, clutter-free space make mealtime safe and much more inviting. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h4)

question: A patient with schizophrenia is leaving the inpatient ward. Which situation means they are NOT ready for a day hospital program?

options.A: They live alone in a supportive family compound
options.B: They attend church services every Sunday with relatives
options.C: They have active homicidal threats and a plan to harm a neighbor
options.D: They take their oral medications reliably every morning

explanation: Spot on! Active danger to others means the patient needs a secure inpatient ward rather than partial care. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why is training community stakeholders so important for health programs?

options.A: It generates financial profit for local hospitals
options.B: It allows them to prescribe pharmaceutical drugs independently
options.C: It turns them into active advocates who champion the cause
options.D: It replaces the need for community health extension workers

explanation: Training empowers leaders with knowledge so they can guide their people and sustain the health program locally. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h4)

question: A 14-year-old pregnant patient faces a high nutritional risk. Why does this happen during her pregnancy?

options.A: Complete resistance to iron supplementation
options.B: Direct competition for nutrients between her growing body and the fetus
options.C: Permanent storage overload of water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Immediate cessation of all bone mineral absorption

explanation: Exactly! Since a young teenager is still growing herself, her body and the baby have to share and compete for limited nutrients. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T8#GNS312_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why is food preservation so important for community health nurses?

options.A: It helps prevent foodborne illness outbreaks and malnutrition
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of operating hospital kitchens
options.C: It is the main way nurses sterilize surgical instruments
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never need dietary supplements

explanation: You'll often teach families about this! Safe food storage protects whole communities from nasty germs and ensures steady nutrition year-round. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h1)

question: Why do vulnerable population groups need special healthcare approaches instead of regular programs?

options.A: Government policy forbids them from visiting general clinics
options.B: They refuse to take any standard orthodox medications
options.C: They face unique barriers like poverty, isolation, and stigma
options.D: Standard programs are too expensive for hospitals to run

explanation: Spot on! Because of hurdles like distance, poverty, or discrimination, standard health programs often fail to reach them without special adjustments. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T28#GNS225_U5_T28_h2)

question: A confused patient arrives at the emergency department with suspected drug ingestion. What quick bedside check must a nurse perform right away?

options.A: Checking blood glucose level
options.B: Measuring abdominal girth
options.C: Testing deep tendon reflexes
options.D: Checking visual acuity

explanation: Always rule out low blood sugar first! Severe hypoglycemia can look identical to a drug overdose, so a quick finger-prick blood glucose check is a nursing essential. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T9#GNS125_U2_T9_h4)

question: What does an Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) tell a nurse administrator?

options.A: The exact percentage of patients who will refuse medication
options.B: The total yearly budget needed to run the emergency department
options.C: The extra cost required to gain one additional unit of health outcome
options.D: The net profit generated by surgical procedures over a quarter

explanation: ICER simply asks: 'Is paying extra for this new treatment worth the extra health benefit we get?' It measures that trade-off. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h4)

question: What usually causes bleeding inside the skull during severe fetal moulding?

options.A: High blood pressure caused by maternal pushing
options.B: Lack of vitamin K in the newborn circulation
options.C: Stretching and tearing of bridging veins inside the skull
options.D: Rupture of scalp arteries from vacuum suction

explanation: Spot on. When the skull bones overlap too severely, they stretch and strain the tiny veins inside, causing them to tear and bleed. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h4)

question: Why should nursing researchers care about national and global health goals?

options.A: It helps secure research funding and ensures the study addresses urgent needs
options.B: It removes all ethical considerations from the research process
options.C: It eliminates the requirement to collect informed consent from patients
options.D: It guarantees that no other nurse will ever read the published paper

explanation: When your research tackles pressing real-world problems, it's easier to get support and make a true difference in society. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why does very little blood flow through the fetal lungs before birth?

options.A: The liver absorbs all the blood first
options.B: The heart pumps too weakly to reach the chest
options.C: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not exchange gas
options.D: Umbilical arteries block the path to the chest

explanation: Since the placenta provides oxygen, the fluid-filled fetal lungs need only minimal blood for nourishment, bypassing the rest. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h1)

question: Which part of a plant is most commonly used in traditional remedies?

options.A: Taproot only
options.B: Pollen grains
options.C: Leaves
options.D: Heartwood

explanation: Leaves are a nurse's and healer's best friend! They are abundant, easy to gather, and grow back quickly without killing the plant. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T2#GNS125_U2_T2_h3)

question: Where do most traditional drug administration abbreviations come from?

options.A: Ancient Greek literature
options.B: Latin terminology
options.C: Modern medical shorthand
options.D: French pharmaceutical guides

explanation: Great job! Most medical abbreviations are rooted in old Latin terms that doctors and pharmacists used historically to describe how drugs should be taken. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why does pregnancy put a woman with sickle cell disease at higher risk for complications?

options.A: Hormones produced during pregnancy destroy normal red blood cells
options.B: The growing uterus completely stops blood flow to the lower extremities
options.C: Pregnancy causes blood volume to rise and the body to clot more easily
options.D: High iron demands in pregnancy cause all hemoglobin to turn into hemoglobin S

explanation: Great thinking! Because pregnancy naturally increases blood volume and clotting tendencies, blocked blood vessels become a bigger risk for these mums. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of taking a nutrition history in nursing practice?

options.A: To gather information about a patient's food intake and eating habits
options.B: To strictly calculate the exact daily financial cost of groceries
options.C: To diagnose rare genetic metabolic disorders immediately
options.D: To prescribe specific medical diets without consulting a doctor

explanation: A nutrition history focuses directly on understanding what and how a patient eats to guide their care. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h1)

question: How do guided slow breathing exercises help a mum going through distress during labour?

options.A: They reduce sympathetic nervous system overdrive and lower anxiety
options.B: They accelerate the dilation of the cervix within minutes
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for any regional anesthesia
options.D: They increase the production of amniotic fluid

explanation: Controlled breathing helps stop hyperventilation, drops those high adrenaline levels, and brings a sense of calm to her body and mind. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h6)

question: What happens to a research study if it lacks a clear conceptual framework?

options.A: It stops patients from participating in the project
options.B: It automatically becomes much easier to complete
options.C: It requires fewer ethical approvals from the committee
options.D: It can easily lose focus and gather irrelevant data

explanation: Without a clear map, you might end up collecting tons of information that doesn't actually help answer your research question. Keep it focused! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h2)

question: Why is an ultrasound or accurate dating so important before giving misoprostol?

options.A: To measure the pelvic muscles for pushing
options.B: To check the patient's exact blood type
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bill
options.D: To rule out an ectopic pregnancy and verify gestational age

explanation: We always double-check that the pregnancy is inside the uterus and within safe limits before starting. Patient safety comes first! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h5)

question: What is a major safety risk when dealing with pressurized gas cylinders as waste?

options.A: Gradual chemical corrosion of plastic containers
options.B: Spread of bacterial infections through the air
options.C: Risk of explosion when exposed to high heat
options.D: Attraction of radioactive dust particles

explanation: Pressurized containers can blow up violently if they get tossed into an incinerator or face extreme heat. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why must you NOT apply suction while pushing the catheter down into the tracheostomy tube?

options.A: It makes the suction machine overheat
options.B: It causes the inner cannula to pop out
options.C: It damages delicate tracheal mucosal tissue
options.D: It pushes secretions deeper into the lungs

explanation: Suctioning on the way in pulls the delicate lining of the windpipe against the catheter tip, causing bleeding and injury. Insert gently first, then suction on the way out! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h5)

question: A nurse manager wants to involve an experienced team of senior nurses in designing a new shift roster. Which style is best?

options.A: Autocratic
options.B: Laissez-faire
options.C: Coercive
options.D: Democratic

explanation: Democratic leadership welcomes staff input and collaboration, making it ideal for planning and problem-solving tasks. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h3)

question: What is the main job of the alveoli in the breast?

options.A: Storing fat to give the breast shape
options.B: Synthesizing and secreting milk
options.C: Producing oxytocin for uterine contractions
options.D: Transporting milk directly to the skin surface

explanation: Spot on! The alveoli are tiny sac-like structures lined with special cells that actually make and secrete milk. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T18#GNS121_U5_T18_h1)

question: What is the main use of Microsoft Word in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Creating animated multimedia presentations for patients
options.B: Drafting clinical documents, policies, and reports
options.C: Analyzing large numeric data sets and statistical formulas
options.D: Storing secure long-term electronic health records

explanation: Think of Microsoft Word as your go-to digital notepad for writing reports, guidelines, and letters! It is built specifically for text documents. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h2)

question: What term describes the complete absence of hydrochloric acid in the stomach?

options.A: Hypercalcemia
options.B: Achlorhydria
options.C: Steatorrhea
options.D: Dyspepsia

explanation: A- (meaning without) + chlorhydria (hydrochloric acid). That's how medical terms break down easily! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which gene mutations are most strongly linked to a higher risk of ovarian cancer?

options.A: BRCA1 and BRCA2
options.B: HER2 and KRAS
options.C: TP53 and EGFR
options.D: APC and MLH1

explanation: Spot on. Inherited mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes significantly increase a woman's lifetime chance of developing both breast and ovarian cancers. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h3)

question: What is the main difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?

options.A: If they come from plants or animals
options.B: The relative quantity the body needs
options.C: Whether they provide any energy at all
options.D: How fast the stomach digests them

explanation: It's all about amount! Macronutrients are needed in large amounts, while micronutrients (like vitamins and minerals) are needed in tiny amounts—though both are equally important for health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T009#GNS227_U1_T009_h3)

question: Which of these everyday body activities is managed by an autonomic reflex?

options.A: Reaching out to pick up a stethoscope
options.B: Deliberate walking across a hospital room
options.C: Changes in heart rate and blood pressure
options.D: Writing patient notes in a chart

explanation: Spot on! Autonomic reflexes quietly run your automatic internal functions—like heart rate and digestion—so you don't have to think about them. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h7)

question: A nurse collects a wound sample using a dirty cotton bud from a desk drawer. What is likely to happen?

options.A: It will turn the culture media bright purple
options.B: It will grow outside contaminants instead of the true wound infection
options.C: It will instantly freeze all bacteria on the cotton tip
options.D: It will cause the laboratory incubator to break down

explanation: Exactly! Unsterilized equipment introduces random environmental germs, which ruins the accuracy of the test results. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why does blowing a gentle, cool breeze from a small fan onto a breathless patient's face help them feel better?

options.A: It dries up excessive oral secretions.
options.B: It increases the percentage of oxygen in room air.
options.C: It stimulates facial nerves that send calming signals to the brain about breathing.
options.D: It lowers the body temperature to cure underlying lung infections.

explanation: Cool air hits the trigeminal nerve on the face, tricking the brain into feeling less breathless. A simple nursing trick that works wonders! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T13#GNS123_U3_T13_h7)

question: When you reach the discussion section of your research, what do you do with your framework?

options.A: Calculating the final financial cost of conducting the study
options.B: Evaluating whether the study findings support or challenge the theory
options.C: Listing all the demographic characteristics of the participants
options.D: Providing a biography of the original nursing theorist

explanation: You got it! In the discussion, you check back in with your framework to see if your results back it up or point to something new. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h6)

question: Which professional does the home health nurse frequently collaborate with to improve patient mobility?

options.A: Radiology technician
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Biomedical engineer
options.D: Hospital pharmacist

explanation: Physical therapists work closely with home health nurses to help patients regain strength, balance, and safe movement at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the correct tool to measure the length of a 14-month-old child?

options.A: A flexible cloth tape measure
options.B: A vertical wall stadiometer
options.C: A hanging spring balance scale
options.D: An infantometer for recumbent length

explanation: Kids under two can't stand straight yet, so we use a flat measuring board (infantometer) while they lie down. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h3)

question: Which situation represents a legal exception where a nurse must break client confidentiality?

options.A: Discussing a patient's laboratory results with a curious neighbor
options.B: Sharing hospital gossip with friends during lunch break
options.C: Posting a photo of an interesting surgical wound on a personal social media page
options.D: Reporting suspected child abuse to the appropriate authorities

explanation: Nurses are legally mandated to breach confidentiality to protect vulnerable individuals from abuse or public health threats. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h5)

question: An autistic patient gets very upset when you shift their routine by just ten minutes. What core feature does this reaction show?

options.A: An intentional attempt to disrupt the ward
options.B: A sign of sudden memory loss
options.C: A rigid adherence to routines and resistance to change
options.D: A lack of basic physical sensation

explanation: It's completely normal for them to feel unsettled here. Predictability brings comfort, so unexpected changes to routines can cause real anxiety. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T5#GNS324_U4_T5_h2)

question: You check a new mother and notice her uterus feels soft and is pushed over to the right side. What should you do first?

options.A: Assist the patient to empty her bladder
options.B: Massage the calves to prevent clots
options.C: Administer a blood transfusion immediately
options.D: Encourage heavy ambulation around the ward

explanation: A full bladder acts like a bully, pushing the uterus upward and to the side and stopping it from contracting properly. Helping her pee often fixes the problem instantly! Great nursing intuition. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: Which of these conditions is NOT linked to problems in the limbic system?

options.A: Major depressive disorder
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Correct! Iron deficiency anemia is a blood and nutrition issue, whereas anxiety, depression, and PTSD are all tied to limbic system imbalances. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h6)

question: A nurse uses a bedside barcode scanner before giving a drug. Which type of informatics does this represent?

options.A: Nursing research informatics
options.B: Consumer health informatics
options.C: Clinical nursing informatics
options.D: Nursing education informatics

explanation: Bedside verification tools directly support clinical workflows and patient safety, placing them squarely in clinical nursing informatics. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h2)

question: A surgical ward notices their wound infection rates jumping up and down wildly every month. What does this suggest?

options.A: The ward has inconsistent infection control practices that put patients at risk
options.B: The nursing staff is following standardized protocols too rigidly
options.C: The laboratory is simply mislabelling routine blood cultures
options.D: The hospital is experiencing normal, safe biological variation in healing

explanation: Well reasoned! Wildly swinging infection rates mean infection control isn't being done the same way every time, putting patients in danger. [learn more](GST319_U2_T4#GST319_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is controlling outside factors so important in explanatory research?

options.A: To guarantee that patients refuse to participate in the study
options.B: To ensure that the observed changes are truly caused by the studied variable
options.C: To hide negative outcomes from the hospital administration
options.D: To make the research process take as long as humanly possible

explanation: You got it! Controlling outside noise makes sure your results genuinely reflect the cause-and-effect you are testing. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which finding strongly suggests a testicular rupture after a heavy blow to the scrotum?

options.A: Painless enlargement of both testicles over a period of several weeks
options.B: Clear watery drainage leaking from a small scratch on the scrotal skin
options.C: Loss of the normal outline of the testicle on ultrasound with severe local tenderness
options.D: Complete inability to control bowel movements after the impact

explanation: When the testicle bursts, it loses its smooth oval shape on an ultrasound scan, and the patient will have intense pain and swelling. You're mastering trauma assessments! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h4)

question: Which country in West Africa has the highest total population?

options.A: Cameroon
options.B: Ghana
options.C: Nigeria
options.D: Senegal

explanation: Spot on! Nigeria is the most populous nation in Africa and drives a lot of the demographic growth in our region. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h1)

question: In research, what do we mean when we say a tool is 'reliable'?

options.A: How easy the questionnaire is for elderly patients to read
options.B: How fast the researcher can collect data from patients
options.C: How consistently the tool produces the same results
options.D: Whether the tool measures what it is supposed to measure

explanation: Think of reliability like a dependable weighing scale—if you step on it five times in a row and get the exact same weight, it's reliable (even if it needs calibration later!). It's all about consistency. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h1)

question: As a bone grows wider, its inner marrow cavity also gets bigger. Which cells are responsible for clearing out the inside?

options.A: Chondrocytes
options.B: Osteoblasts
options.C: Osteoclasts
options.D: Osteocytes

explanation: Think of osteoclasts as the cleaning crew—they dissolve bone along the inner wall so the marrow cavity can expand as the bone gets thicker outside. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T1#GNS121_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which nursing action best helps a patient who is trying to overcome avoidance behaviors triggered by anxiety?

options.A: Supporting gradual exposure to feared situations
options.B: Encouraging deeper regression into dependent behaviors
options.C: Isolating the patient until anxiety disappears completely
options.D: Telling the patient to ignore all feelings of fear

explanation: Taking small, supported steps toward what scares them helps patients build confidence and rewrite their brain's alarm system safely. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h7)

question: A nurse notices that a postoperative surgical wound is increasingly red, warm, and draining foul-smelling pus. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the patient's scheduled discharge day to mention it
options.B: Assume this is a normal healing process and take no action
options.C: Report the findings and document them clearly for the care team
options.D: Apply a dry bandage and advise the patient not to look at it

explanation: Prompt reporting and documentation ensure the medical team can investigate and treat a potential surgical site infection early. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: A patient on a low-calorie diet complains of feeling dizzy and weak all the time. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Ignore the complaints as normal adjustment
options.B: Assess current intake and report symptoms
options.C: Tell the patient to stop drinking all water
options.D: Advise the patient to cut calories further

explanation: Spot on! Dizziness and fatigue could mean the patient's diet is too restrictive or causing low blood sugar, so you need to assess them right away. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T010#GNS227_U6_T010_h6)

question: On which side of the body should a patient hold a single-point walking cane?

options.A: Alternating hands with every step
options.B: Always in the dominant hand
options.C: The weak side of the body
options.D: The strong side of the body

explanation: Holding the cane on the strong side allows the patient to lean weight onto the device while moving the weaker leg forward. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why should you avoid using tweezers to pull out a honeybee stinger?

options.A: Tweezers are too sharp and will cut the patient's epidermis
options.B: Squeezing can push more venom from the attached sac into the skin
options.C: It causes the stinger to dissolve inside the wound
options.D: Metal reacts chemically with insect venom to cause burns

explanation: Spot on! Pinching with tweezers squeezes the attached venom sac like a bulb syringe, pumping even more toxin straight into the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T12#GNS221_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the best sign that an intersectoral health program is truly sustainable?

options.A: The federal government takes over all local day-to-day management
options.B: The community takes ownership and maintains the project after external support ends
options.C: Foreign donors continue funding the program for at least twenty years
options.D: The local clinic stops seeing patients and focuses only on administrative reports

explanation: Well done! True sustainability means the community is strong enough to keep things running locally all by themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h7)

question: What actually happens during an autoimmune response?

options.A: Red blood cells begin attacking invading bacteria
options.B: The immune system mistakenly attacks healthy body tissues
options.C: The body stops producing white blood cells completely
options.D: Foreign invaders rapidly multiply without any immune resistance

explanation: Autoimmunity happens when the immune system gets confused and treats our own healthy cells like dangerous enemies. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which category of healthcare waste includes discarded scalpels and broken glass ampoules?

options.A: Sharps
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste
options.C: Pathological waste
options.D: General waste

explanation: Sharps are any objects that can puncture or cut skin, including needles, surgical blades, and broken glass vials. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h2)

question: You see an infected villager walking toward the local drinking pond to soothe a burning leg blister. What should you do first?

options.A: Stop the person from entering the water and provide safe filtered water
options.B: Advise the villager to wash the wound thoroughly inside the well
options.C: Pull the entire Guinea worm out rapidly with surgical forceps
options.D: Administer a strong dose of oral antibiotics to kill the worm

explanation: Fantastic nursing judgment! Keeping infected limbs out of community water sources stops the transmission cycle right in its tracks. You're going to make an amazing nurse! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h8)

question: What is the main difference between blood plasma and serum?

options.A: Plasma is found outside blood vessels while serum is found inside
options.B: Plasma contains red blood cells while serum contains only white blood cells
options.C: Serum lacks clotting proteins like fibrinogen because it has already clotted
options.D: Serum has a much higher water content than plasma

explanation: Spot on! Think of serum as plasma that has finished doing its clotting job; the clotting proteins (like fibrinogen) get used up during the clot, leaving serum behind. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T1#GNS311_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a good quality for a clinical recommendation based on research data?

options.A: Being directly supported by the findings of the study
options.B: Being clear and easy for frontline nurses to understand
options.C: Being realistic about the equipment available in the clinic
options.D: Being completely unrealistic and impossible for staff to carry out

explanation: Good recommendations must be practical. If a guideline is impossible to carry out on a real ward, busy clinical staff will simply ignore it. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why must researchers clean their data before presenting the results?

options.A: To convert all qualitative words into numbers
options.B: To ensure the study meets word count requirements
options.C: To prevent errors from distorting the final findings
options.D: To make the statistical analysis completely unnecessary

explanation: Checking for missing values and errors beforehand ensures that the data presentation reflects true clinical realities rather than mistakes. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h1)

question: How do the four scales of measurement relate to one another?

options.A: Lower scales are more accurate than higher ratio scales

question: A patient is assessed as a high fall risk. Which nursing action is best to keep them safe?

question: What is a common body composition trap for older adults whose BMI looks completely normal?

question: What is a major advantage of using topical NSAIDs instead of oral NSAIDs for older adults with osteoarthritis?

question: As a student nurse doing chest compressions, how do you make sure blood keeps filling the heart between pushes?

question: Why is handing project ownership over to local community members crucial for sustainability?

question: A mother brings in her infant who is very sleepy (lethargic) and vomiting everything she feeds her. According to IMCI, what do these signs mean?

question: In the popular SBAR communication tool used by healthcare workers, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

question: An inspector visits a restaurant and finds rotten food right next to fresh vegetables. What is the best immediate action?

question: When food prices shoot up due to inflation, how do many families change what they eat?

question: What is the main reason we use diagnostic devices in healthcare?

question: A patient has worried endlessly about money for over a year and now feels constantly exhausted and sick. Which GAS stage is this?

question: A nursing unit notices halfway through the year that their infection control goal is off track. What should happen next in the MBO cycle?

question: A nurse wants to study past unconscious ICU dreams, but no records exist. Which research requirement is missing?

question: Why should a nurse avoid documenting subjective opinions like 'patient is lying about how she got these bruises' in a clinical chart?

options.B: Because clinical records require objective facts and direct quotes for legal validity

question: Why is tiopronin often preferred over D-penicillamine in modern practice?

question: A patient is admitted with suspected Neisseria meningitidis. What precautions should you start right away?

options.A: Reverse isolation to protect the patient from others

options.C: Strict airborne precautions in a negative pressure room
options.D: Droplet precautions

question: How are audit findings usually summarized when presenting to management?

question: What is the main way frontline nurses and midwives help with tracking maternal mortality?

question: What do collagen fibers mainly give to our bones?

question: The QA committee notices nurses are struggling with children's drug dosage calculations. What is the best step to take?

question: Why do nurses and researchers use a scatter diagram?

question: Your patient just had talc pleurodesis and is crying out in sharp pain. What is your very first nursing action?

question: What is the main purpose of MeSH terms in healthcare databases?

question: What is the primary focus of community mobilisation for mental health?

question: What is the purpose of antimicrobial sensitivity testing?

question: How do nurses act as a bridge in disaster response networks?

question: Why is asking patients about their ability to afford basic needs important during a clinical assessment?

question: Why do airborne diseases require special negative-pressure rooms while droplet diseases do not?

question: Why is vitamin K given as an injection to a newborn baby?

question: Why must a nurse check that a patient hasn't eaten or drunk anything (NPO status) before a scheduled laryngoscopy?

question: Why do we always send a written referral form when moving a patient from a primary clinic to a big teaching hospital?

question: How can tele-nursing work best in rural areas with limited resources?

question: What is the main goal of data protection laws like the NDPR in healthcare?

options.D: ARBs act exclusively on the central nervous system instead of blood vessels

explanation: You nailed it! While ACE inhibitors stop angiotensin II from being made in the first place, ARBs let it form but block it from attaching to its receptor targets. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T2#GNS223_U1_T2_h4)

question: A community health nurse notices that pregnant women in her area always arrive late with severe complications. What is the best proactive step to take?

options.A: Wait until the government builds a new tertiary hospital nearby
options.B: Report the patients to local traditional rulers for punishment
options.C: Refuse to treat patients who arrive after their expected due date
options.D: Conduct community education on pregnancy danger signs and early clinic attendance

explanation: Proactive education is key! Teaching women about danger signs before complications arise helps them recognize trouble early and come to the clinic on time. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h8)

question: When should discharge planning ideally start in primary nursing?

options.A: When the patient complains about high hospital bills
options.B: Right upon the patient's admission to the unit
options.C: Only after the doctor signs the official discharge papers
options.D: On the exact morning the patient is scheduled to leave

explanation: Smart nursing! We start planning for home the very minute the patient walks through the door so nothing is rushed at the end. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h3)

question: What kind of metabolic shift is typically triggered by major trauma, severe burns, or sepsis?

options.A: Metabolic dormancy
options.B: Hypermetabolic state
options.C: Basal stabilization
options.D: Hypometabolic hibernation

explanation: 'Hyper' means high! Severe physical stress forces the body into overdrive to fight off infection and heal wounds quickly. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h6)

question: A low-income family avoids visiting the clinic for malaria because of lack of cash. What is the most likely long-term result?

options.A: The illness worsens, potentially leading to severe complications and catastrophic spending later
options.B: The local government refunds all transportation costs to the hospital
options.C: The family automatically qualifies for free federal government healthcare
options.D: The community health insurance scheme covers the full bill retroactively

explanation: Delaying care due to direct costs often results in advanced disease stages that require expensive emergency treatment, pushing families deeper into poverty. This is why financial protection in health is so vital! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h3)

question: A nursing mother complains of painful swelling and redness in only her left calf. What should you do?

options.A: Advise her to apply hot compresses and stay in bed for three days
options.B: Prescribe oral iron supplements for suspected postpartum anaemia
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal muscular strain from carrying the baby
options.D: Refer her urgently for suspected deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Pain and swelling in just one leg is a warning sign of a blood clot (DVT). It needs an urgent hospital check to keep her safe! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h2)

question: Which international declaration in 1978 made Primary Health Care the main strategy for global health?

options.A: The Alma-Ata Declaration
options.B: The Geneva Nursing Charter
options.C: The Lagos Health Accord
options.D: The London Sanitary Treaty

explanation: Remember Alma-Ata! The 1978 conference put Primary Health Care on the map as the key to health for everyone. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is tele-nursing mainly all about?

options.A: The training of nursing students through online video lectures
options.B: A computerized machine that automatically administers medications
options.C: An online filing system used strictly for hospital record keeping
options.D: The practice of nursing care delivered over a distance using technology

explanation: You got this! Tele-nursing simply means using phones, video calls, or apps to connect with patients remotely, giving them guidance and support without needing to be right beside them. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why do nurse managers create a duty roster?

options.A: Ensuring 24-hour ward coverage without overworking staff
options.B: Determining the exact annual budget for the hospital
options.C: Punishing nurses who arrive late to work
options.D: Deciding which medications to purchase from vendors

explanation: A good duty roster makes sure patients are well cared for around the clock while keeping nurses fresh and preventing burnout. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of disaster 'mitigation'?

options.A: Treating injured survivors in a hospital emergency room
options.B: Broadcasting breaking news of a collapsed building
options.C: Enforcing building codes in flood-prone areas
options.D: Distributing blankets to displaced families in a camp

explanation: Well done! Mitigation is all about taking action *before* disaster strikes to reduce risk and prevent harm—like making sure buildings can withstand floods. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why do doctors start checking for fertility issues after just six months for women aged 35 and older?

options.A: To account for the faster decline in ovarian reserve and egg quality
options.B: Because older couples have more frequent sexual intercourse
options.C: To prevent the development of chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Because hormonal treatments work much faster in older women

explanation: Spot on! Egg quality and quantity change faster as women get older, so catching things early helps. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T19#GNS312_U1_T19_h1)
